newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras content with world coffee price spike.
newsitem.headline: Honduras content with world coffee price spike.

text.p: Honduras coffee exporters expressed contentment Friday at the recent spike in world prices.

"We are very happy with the spike in international coffee markets in the last two weeks, because these prices have not been seen for the last two and a half years," Osmond Maduro, the head of the Honduras Coffee Exporters Assocation said.
"If the price stays in a range around $140 (per 100-lb quintal) we will have obtained foreign exchange earnings of $350 million from this harvest," Maduro told reporters.
Coffee is the biggest export and hard currency earner for the Central American nation.
Honduras produced 3 million 100-lb (46-kg) bags of coffee in the last 1995-1996 cycle, exporting 2.6 million bags for around $280 million, according to the Honduras Coffee Growers Association.
Predictions from the state-run Honduran Coffee Institute (Icafe) are for the current 1996-1997 harvest to fall 500,000 46-kg bags to 2.5 million quintals because of rains during crucial flowerings.
Honduras has 85,000 coffee growers across 14 of the country's 18 states.
